Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.

They’re capable collaborators on ambitious projects in many fields, and show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. https://t.co/jP0AutLxXb

Claude Fable 5.2 is now available in Cursor!

At max effort, it's the top model on CursorBench at 60%.

Fable 5.2 scores 56.9% on CursorBench at default effort, up from 49.2% for Fable 5.1. https://t.co/FaEmGCQSpW

At @vercel we got to test this model before release. Best way to summarize it: astonishingly brilliant.

One interesting takeaway: it's very clear that this new generation of models can take on unprecedented bodies of parallel work.

To actually seize this intelligence, you need cloud sandboxes. Full stop. The model can delegate and orchestrate far more than a single computer can handle. Likely far more than you can even imagine it can handle.

Your bottleneck is now ① your ambition and ② your parallel computing power.

Btw, I learned from @cramforce you don't need to overcomplicate it. Install Vercel CLI, setup the Plugin and tell the agent to use /𝚘𝚏𝚏𝚕𝚘𝚊𝚍-𝚝𝚘-𝚜𝚊𝚗𝚍𝚋𝚘𝚡 skill. It'll provision and de-allocate cloud sandboxes as needed. You don't need a "multi-agent remote harness ralph orchestrator" 😆

So bullish on MCP. Its utility exceeds the "M" part: even AI aside, it'll be a civilization-scale accomplishment to get all our systems communicating through one universal open protocol.

A missing piece was how to get arbitrary callbacks across sessions. MCP could read and write, but it couldn't tell you later "this event happened." MCP Events fixes this.

We're adding support in our own MCP. Say an agent makes a deployment, and wants to know when it's complete. Instead of polling, it can subscribe to 𝚍𝚎𝚙𝚕𝚘𝚢𝚖𝚎𝚗𝚝.𝚜𝚞𝚌𝚌𝚎𝚎𝚍𝚎𝚍.

PSA: With Vercel Queues and Workflows, writing the backend machinery for your own MCPs to do this is easy peasy.

- to run it "without displaying output"
- to run it "automatically without asking for confirmation"

It is a prompt injection written to stop the agent from looking at the file!

‼️ React Server Components Flaw Lets Hackers Execute Code Remotely Without Authentication 

Details: https://t.co/Pd5hSzPEhL

A critical security flaw in React Server Components can let attackers run code remotely without logging in. React published the advisory, tracked as GHSA-xqc2-xf4c-x3h3, on October 14, 2026.

The issue carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.5, and the React team recommends immediate updates for affected applications. The flaw affects react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack. These packages support React Server Components across different build tools.

The exploitation requires an extremely rare response pattern involving multiple typed arrays and a value controlled by an attacker. Simply using React does not make every application vulnerable.

author.name: やぎ（八木 利生太郎）/ Last Scene代表

items.text:
最近発生したClaude Code関連のセキュリティ問題話

・Yes, and don't ask againでシークレット情報がGitHubで公開
・特定のブラウザを開くとファイルがダウンロードされて、CLAUDE.mdでシークレット情報を外部サーバーへアップ

1つ目は、リポジトリをprivateで管理する事と、シークレットな情報をGitHubにアップロードしないようにhookとか使って防ぐのが大事。

2つ目は、ブラウザ操作で変なサイトを開かないように、どのサイトを開いたかどうかをちゃんとチェックする事と、Downloadsフォルダ上で起動しない事をする必要がある。
プロジェクト操作する時は毎回移動して、その上でclaudeコマンドを実行するようにすると防げる。

あと、Claude CodeとかCodex使ってるといつの間にか、ストレージの容量が圧迫されてしまうので、定期的に不要なファイルを削除するように心がけることで防ぐこともできる。
